A human would use both hands with palms up to trace a large, horizontal circle in front of their torso, then push their hands forward to present the "bowl".

P1: `dir: "up"`, `gripper_orientation: "horizontal"`. This mimics a palm-up gesture, as if supporting the bowl from underneath. P2: `dir: "front"`, `gripper_orientation: "vertical"`. This mimics cupping the side of the bowl. Winner: P1 is superior because it more clearly communicates "supporting the weight" of a large object from its base, which is a primary characteristic of a bowl.
# Q3: Structure Comparison. Compare 2+ primitive sequences (e.g., M1: pose > path arc vs M2: pose > movement rep). State the winner and why.
M1: Pose (start) > Path Arc (trace rim) > Pose (hold) > Movement (push forward). This sequence clearly separates defining the object's shape, establishing it with a pause, and then acting on it. M2: Pose (center) > Path Arc (trace half) > Path Arc (trace other half). This only forms the shape but lacks the interaction of presenting it. Winner: M1 tells a clearer story: "Here is a large bowl (trace & hold), and I am giving it to you (push)."

A1: Add a brief hold after tracing the arc. This pause allows the viewer to register the "bowl" before the next action begins, solidifying the object's existence in space. A2: Add a slight "lift" (z-axis move) after the arc. This suggests picking up the bowl before presenting it. Winner: A1 is better because a simple pause is a classic mime technique to establish an object; adding a lift might be too much motion and could confuse the primary gesture.
